newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money starts week mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: German call money starts week mostly unchanged.

text.p: German overnight funds kicked off the new week's activities trading mostly steady between 2.95 and three percent as liquidity conditions remained ample on Monday.
"Trading is fairly dull and call money has been trading right where it was at the end of last week," one senior trader at a Frankfurt-based bank said.

Dealers said the bulk of trades was being conducted around 2.97 percent but added they did not expect rates to fall much further in the coming sessions. "Liquidity conditions are still good, but I don't see rates falling more," another dealer said.
With bank reserves considered mostly ample, dealers said there was little need to worry about tricky month end conditions.
On the other hand, dealers also said it was premature to speculate on what the Bundesbank might do at this week's tender operation.

Banks held 40.2 billion marks in reserves at the Bundesbank on Friday, up from Thursday's 39.1 billion marks. Average reserve holdings for the month remained unchanged at 40.2 billion marks and Lombard borrowings were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate FIONA= was set at 3.01400 percent compared with 3.01333 percent on Friday.
